responsibility: Implements the core AVR GCC backend: target hooks, RTL expansion/output support, costing, calling convention logic, address-space handling, section and symbol encoding, prologue/epilogue generation, builtin expansion, and many AVR-specific helper routines referenced from the machine description. This is the main target implementation file that owns how GCC lowers generic code to AVR RTL and assembly, including flash/RAM address-space semantics, register usage, instruction length adjustment, library-call conventions, and registration of the AVR hook table in `targetm`.
same_name_distinction: This is the executable C++ implementation for the AVR port: unlike avr.h it defines the backend behavior, unlike avr.md it provides the helper functions and target-hook code that machine-description patterns rely on, and unlike avr.opt it consumes the parsed AVR options to implement their effects.
